stem: A newborn has hypotonia, upslanting palpebral fissures, a single palmar crease and a protruding tongue. Which diagnosis best fits these findings?
explanation: Hypotonia, upslanting palpebral fissures, a single palmar crease and a protruding tongue are typical clinical features of Down syndrome, most commonly caused by trisomy 21.
